review_notes: I read the whole file and the Path.lean simp set (length_nil, length_cons, length_comp are all simp). I read the only external use of the cast lemmas, in Covering.lean (lines 195-226), and grepped Mathlib for `length_cast` and other cast lemmas (none exist). I could not run Lean, so I did not check whether the proposed lemmas would work as simp lemmas. I found no loops in the existing simp lemmas: cast_rfl_rfl, cast_cast and cast_nil all simplify toward fewer casts. The two findings are about missing coverage, and both are moderate. The simp-set effects of `Path.cast_cons` would need to be checked.

findings.excerpt: (p.cons e).cast hu hw = (p.cast hu rfl).cons (e.cast rfl hw)
findings.problem: This is the cast-normalising rule for `cons`, but it is not simp. Together with the simp lemmas `cast_nil`, `cast_rfl_rfl` and `cast_cast`, it would reduce casts to the leaves. As the file stands, `(p.cons e).cast hu hw` is a stuck simp normal form. The only use, in Covering.lean, calls `rw [..., Path.cast_cons, Path.cast_rfl_rfl]` by hand, so the pair is already applied as a unit. The rewrite terminates, because the cast moves onto strictly smaller paths and arrows. Its RHS contains `Path.cast ... rfl` and `Hom.cast rfl ...`, which the existing simp lemmas can clean up.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `Path.cast_cons` with `@[simp]`, so that `cast_rfl_rfl` can clean up the `rfl` casts it produces. Alternatively, keep it non-simp and say in the docstring that it is the intended rewrite. The Covering.lean `rw [..., Path.cast_cons, Path.cast_rfl_rfl]` calls could then become `simp`.
findings.benefit: Casts of paths built with `cons` would simplify to `cons` of casts, which is what the `cast_nil`, `cast_rfl_rfl` and `cast_cast` simp lemmas are meant to reach. Users would not have to remember to `rw [Path.cast_cons]` before the other simp lemmas apply.

findings.excerpt: def Path.cast {u v u' v' : U} (hu : u = u') (hv : v = v') (p : Path u v) : Path u' v' :=
findings.problem: `Path.length` has a full simp interface (`length_nil`, `length_cons`, `length_toPath` and `length_comp` are all simp). The file introduces `Path.cast` and simp lemmas for `cast_nil`, `cast_cast` and `cast_rfl_rfl`, but it has no simp lemma saying that casting preserves length. `(p.cast hu hv).length` is stuck for simp when `hu` and `hv` are not `rfl`, because `Eq.ndrec` can't be reduced on variable equalities. The file's last theorem already needs `length` and `cast` together, and grepping Mathlib shows no `length_cast` anywhere.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem Path.length_cast (hu : u = u') (hv : v = v') (p : Path u v) : (p.cast hu hv).length = p.length`, proved by `subst_vars; rfl`. Place it after `Path.cast_rfl_rfl`, with the other simp lemmas.
findings.benefit: `simp` can then see through casts when it reasons about path lengths, and `length_cons`, `length_nil` and `length_comp` stay usable after casts are introduced. This avoids ad hoc `subst`-and-`rfl` proofs.
